questions.text: अंगूर के पौधों में प्रतानों की वृद्धि निम्नलिखित के कारण होती है :
questions.text_english: The growth of tendrils in grapes plants is due to :

options.C: अवलम्ब (आधार) के संपर्क में आई प्रतान (प्ररोह) कोशिकाओं में त्वरित कोशिका विभाजन
options.D: अवलम्ब संपर्क की सतह से विपरीत (परे) प्रतान (प्ररोह) कोशिकाओं में त्वरित कोशिका विभाजन

options_english.C: Rapid cell division in tendril cells in contact with the support
options_english.D: Rapid cell division in tendril cells that are away from the support

questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Tendril growth in grape plants occurs due to a phenomenon called thigmotropism. When a tendril touches a support, the cells on the side away from the support divide faster than those in contact with the support. This differential cell division causes the tendril to curl around the support, enabling the plant to climb. Option (A) is incorrect as light drives phototropism, not tendril coiling. Option (B) is incorrect as gravity drives geotropism. Option (C) is incorrect because it is the cells away from the support, not in contact, that divide rapidly.

questions.text: मानव में अवायवीय श्वसन प्रक्रम से संबंधित कुछ अभिलक्षणों की सूची प्रवीन को निम्न तालिका के रूप में दी गई : अवस्थिति — (i) पेशी कोशिका, परिस्थिति — (ii) ऑक्सीजन (O2) तथा कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (CO2) की उपस्थिति की आवश्यकता, अंत्योत्पाद — (iii) 3-कार्बन अणु। उपर्युक्त अभिलक्षणों में से कौन-सा/से अभिलक्षण उपर्युक्त प्रक्रम से संबंधित है/हैं ?
questions.text_english: Pravin was given a list of characteristics associated with the process of anaerobic respiration in humans — Location: (i) Muscle Cell; Condition: (ii) Requires presence of Oxygen (O2) and Carbon dioxide (CO2); End Product: (iii) 3-Carbon molecules. Which of the above characteristics is/are related to the above process ?
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells occurs in the muscle cells themselves — so (i) is correct. It does NOT require oxygen; instead it occurs in the absence of oxygen — so (ii) is incorrect. The end product of anaerobic respiration in humans is lactic acid, which is a 3-carbon molecule — so (iii) is correct. Therefore characteristics (i) and (iii) are correctly associated with anaerobic respiration in humans.

questions.text: उच्चतर पोषी स्तर के जीव जो निम्नतर पोषी स्तर से संबंधित अनेक प्रकार के जीवों को खाते हैं, मिलकर बनाते हैं :
questions.text_english: Organisms of a higher trophic level which feed on several types of organisms belonging to a lower trophic level form the :
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. A food web is formed when organisms at a higher trophic level feed on multiple types of organisms from a lower trophic level. This creates interconnected feeding relationships, as opposed to a simple linear food chain (D), which represents a single sequence of feeding. An ecosystem (B) refers to all living and non-living components of an environment, and an ecological pyramid (C) is a graphical representation of trophic levels — neither of these represents the interconnected feeding pattern described.

options_english.A: Both plants are kept in the dark room for three days before placing them in separate glass jars.
options_english.B: Both plants are covered with separate wooden bell-jars.
options_english.C: Use vaseline to seal the bottom of the jars with the glass plates.
options_english.D: Both potted plants were kept in sunlight for a few hours before the iodine test for the presence of starch.

questions.image_description: Two potted plants each covered with a bell-jar. Plant (I) has a watch-glass containing potassium hydroxide inside the jar. Plant (II) has no KOH. The bell-jars are sealed at the bottom with glass plates and vaseline.
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct — it is the incorrect step. In this experiment to demonstrate that CO2 is necessary for photosynthesis, the bell-jars must be made of glass (transparent), not wood. Wooden bell-jars would block sunlight from reaching the plant, preventing photosynthesis from occurring regardless of CO2 availability. The other steps — destarch the plants in darkness (A), seal jars with vaseline (C), and keep in sunlight before iodine test (D) — are all correct procedures for this activity.

questions.text: किसी पारितंत्र में आहार श्रृंखला के माध्यम से उच्चतर पोषी स्तर में हानिकारक (विषैले) पदार्थों के संचयन में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से जीव सर्वाधिक प्रभावित होते हैं ?
questions.text_english: In accumulation of toxic substances at higher trophic levels of an ecosystem through the food chain, which of the following organisms is affected the most ?
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The phenomenon described is biological magnification (biomagnification). Toxic substances like pesticides are not metabolised or excreted; they accumulate and become more concentrated at each successive trophic level. Human beings occupy the highest trophic level in most food chains (aquatic plants → small fish → large fish → humans), so they accumulate the greatest concentration of toxic substances and are affected the most. Small aquatic plants (A) have the lowest concentration as they are at the base of the chain.

questions.text: किसी पुष्प में लैंगिक जनन की घटनाओं को निम्नलिखित में से किसमें सही अनुक्रम में निरूपित किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of events of sexual reproduction in a flower ?
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. The correct sequence of events in sexual reproduction in a flower is: first, Pollination (transfer of pollen from anther to stigma); then Fertilization (fusion of male gamete with the egg cell); then the Embryo develops from the zygote; and finally the Seed is formed enclosing the embryo. Option (A) is incorrect as Embryo cannot come after Seed. Options (B) and (C) are entirely reversed or incorrect sequences.

questions.text: जीवाणु (बैक्टीरिया) जनित लैंगिक संचारित रोग है :
questions.text_english: The sexually transmitted disease caused by bacteria is :
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted disease (STD) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae. AIDS (B) is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), which is a virus, not a bacterium. Diarrhoea (A) is caused by various pathogens including bacteria like Vibrio cholerae, but it is not an STD. Warts (D) are caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV), a virus. Hence, Gonorrhoea is the only bacterial STD among the given options.

Assertion (A) : Arteries have valves as they have to withstand high pressure.
Reason (R) : Arteries are vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs.
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. The Assertion (A) is FALSE: arteries do NOT have valves. Arteries have thick, elastic, muscular walls to withstand the high blood pressure of blood pumped from the heart — but it is VEINS (not arteries) that have valves, to prevent backflow of blood moving against gravity back to the heart. The Reason (R) is TRUE: arteries are indeed blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.

questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Microbes such as bacteria and fungi act as decomposers — they break down the dead organic matter and waste products of organisms, releasing nutrients back into the soil. Without microbes, this decomposition would not occur and the soil would lose its fertility over time, confirming the Assertion.

questions.text_english:
What are hormones ? State any one function of the following hormones :
(i) Insulin
(ii) Adrenaline

key_points: Hormones are chemical substances secreted by endocrine glands directly into the blood.
Insulin: secreted by pancreas; regulates blood glucose level by promoting conversion of glucose to glycogen in liver.
Adrenaline: secreted by adrenal glands; prepares body for 'fight or flight' response by increasing heart rate, breathing rate and blood pressure.

questions.solution: Hormones are chemical substances (chemical messengers) secreted in very small amounts by endocrine glands directly into the bloodstream. They regulate and coordinate the activities of various organs and tissues of the body. Function of Insulin: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas. It lowers the blood glucose level by promoting the conversion of excess glucose into glycogen in the liver and muscles. Function of Adrenaline: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands during situations of fear, stress, or excitement. It increases the heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure, preparing the body for a 'fight or flight' response.

questions.text:
(i) ओजोन परत के अवक्षय के लिए क्लोरोफ्लुओरोकार्बनों (CFCs) को मुख्य कारक माना गया है। 1987 में, संयुक्त राष्ट्र पर्यावरण कार्यक्रम (UNEP) में सर्वानुमति बनाने में सफलता मिली। इस सर्वानुमति का उल्लेख कीजिए।
(ii) हमारे वायुमंडल में ओजोन की क्या भूमिका है ?
questions.text_english:
(i) Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) have been linked to depletion of ozone layer. In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) succeeded in making an agreement. State this agreement.
(ii) What is the role of ozone in our atmosphere ?

key_points: The 1987 UNEP agreement is the Montreal Protocol — countries agreed to freeze production of CFCs at 1986 levels and to progressively reduce and phase out CFCs.
Ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, preventing it from reaching the Earth's surface and protecting living organisms from its harmful effects.

questions.solution: The 1987 UNEP agreement is called the Montreal Protocol. Under this agreement, countries agreed to freeze the production of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) at 1986 levels and to progressively reduce and eventually phase out the production and use of CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances. The role of ozone in our atmosphere is to absorb the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation coming from the sun. The ozone layer in the stratosphere acts as a shield, preventing this dangerous UV radiation from reaching the Earth's surface, thereby protecting all living organisms from its harmful effects such as skin cancer and eye damage.

questions.text: किस प्रकार का श्वसन अधिक ऊर्जा प्रदान करता है और क्यों ?
questions.text_english: What kind of respiration provides more energy and why ?

key_points: Aerobic respiration provides more energy.
In aerobic respiration, glucose is completely oxidised in the presence of oxygen to CO2 and water, releasing 38 ATP molecules per glucose molecule.
In anaerobic respiration, glucose is incompletely broken down releasing only 2 ATP molecules, as the process is incomplete.

questions.solution: Aerobic respiration provides much more energy than anaerobic respiration. In aerobic respiration, glucose is completely oxidised in the presence of oxygen into carbon dioxide and water. This complete breakdown releases a large amount of energy — approximately 38 ATP molecules per glucose molecule. In anaerobic respiration, glucose is only partially broken down (into lactic acid in muscles, or ethanol and CO2 in yeast) in the absence of oxygen. Since the breakdown is incomplete, far less energy — only 2 ATP molecules per glucose molecule — is released. Hence, aerobic respiration is far more efficient and provides more energy.

questions.text: जब मेंडल ने मटर के शुद्ध लंबे पौधे का मटर के शुद्ध बौने पौधे के साथ संकरण कराया, तो उसके F1 पीढ़ी में प्राप्त क्रॉस तथा संतति में प्रेक्षित परिणामों को दर्शाइए।
questions.text_english: Show the cross and observations made by Mendel when he crossed pure tall pea plant with a pure short pea plant to get F1 progeny.

key_points: Parent cross: TT (pure tall) × tt (pure dwarf)
F1 progeny: All Tt — all plants are tall (100% tall)
Tallness (T) is dominant over dwarfness (t) which is recessive
Observation: All F1 plants appeared tall; the dwarf character was not expressed but was carried in a hidden (recessive) form

questions.solution:
When Mendel crossed a pure tall pea plant (TT) with a pure dwarf pea plant (tt), the cross can be shown as follows:

Parents: TT (Pure Tall) × tt (Pure Dwarf)
Gametes: T, T from tall parent; t, t from dwarf parent
F1 Progeny: All plants are Tt (Tall)

Observations: All plants in the F1 generation were tall. The dwarf character completely disappeared in the F1 generation. Mendel observed that tallness was dominant over dwarfness — the trait that appeared in F1 was called the dominant trait (tallness), and the trait that did not appear was called the recessive trait (dwarfness). The recessive trait was not lost but was present in a hidden, unexpressed form in all F1 plants.

questions.text_english:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Herbivores have a longer small intestine.
(b) Inner lining of small intestine has numerous finger-like projections.
(c) Rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is much faster than that in terrestrial organisms.

key_points: (a) Herbivores eat plant material (cellulose) which is difficult to digest; a longer intestine provides more time and surface area for complete digestion.
(b) Finger-like projections called villi increase the surface area for absorption of digested food into the bloodstream.
(c) Dissolved oxygen content in water is very low; aquatic organisms must breathe faster to obtain sufficient oxygen from water.

questions.solution:
(a) Herbivores eat plant material which is rich in cellulose. Cellulose is a complex carbohydrate that is difficult to digest and requires more time for digestion. Therefore, herbivores have a longer small intestine to allow sufficient time and surface area for the complete digestion and absorption of nutrients from the plant material.

(b) The inner lining of the small intestine has numerous finger-like projections called villi. These villi greatly increase the surface area available for the absorption of digested food (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids) into the blood and lymph vessels. A greater surface area ensures faster and more efficient absorption.

(c) Water contains a very low amount of dissolved oxygen compared to air. Aquatic organisms therefore need to process large amounts of water through their gills rapidly in order to extract sufficient oxygen. This is why their breathing rate is much faster compared to terrestrial organisms, which breathe air that has a much higher concentration of oxygen.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित परिच्छेद को पढ़िए तथा उसके नीचे दिए गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :

सभी पौधों में प्रकाश-संश्लेषण की क्रियाविधि एकसमान नहीं होती। अधिकतर पौधों में, यह गैसीय कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड पर निर्भर करती है जो सीधे पत्तियों में विसरित हो जाती है। परन्तु, कुछ पौधों में कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड पत्तियों की कोशिकाओं की रिक्तिकाओं में जटिल कार्बन यौगिक के भाग के रूप में भण्डारित हो सकती है। यह यौगिक क्लोरोप्लास्ट में स्थानांतरित हो जाता है और प्रकाश-संश्लेषण प्रक्रिया के लिए आवश्यकतानुसार कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड को मुक्त करता है। ऐसा माना जाता है कि इस विशेष प्रणाली का विकास उन पौधों में अनुकूलन के परिणामस्वरूप हुआ है जिनके रंध्र (स्टोमेटा) दिन में नहीं खुलते हैं, ताकि जल का संरक्षण हो सके और वे शुष्क (मरुस्थलीय) परिस्थितियों में जीवित रह सकें।

(क) अथवा (ख) में से किसी एक का उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :

Not all plants carry out photosynthesis by the same mechanism. In most plants, it depends directly on gaseous carbon dioxide that diffuses into the leaf. However, some plants can store carbon dioxide in the vacuole of the leaf cells as part of a complex carbon compound. This compound is transported to the chloroplast and releases carbon dioxide when required for photosynthesis. This special mechanism is believed to have evolved as an adaptation in such plants which do not open stomata during the daytime to conserve water for survival in dry conditions (desert conditions).

Attempt either (a) or (b) :
questions.instruction_line: (क) अथवा (ख) में से किसी एक का उत्तर दीजिए।

sub_questions.text:
(क) (i) शुष्क परिस्थितियों में जीवित रहने के लिए इन पौधों में कौन-सा प्रक्रम पौधे की सहायतार्थ न्यूनतम दर से कार्य करता है ?
(ii) प्रकाश-संश्लेषण की अवधि में पत्ती का कौन-सा भाग गैसों के विनिमय के लिए उत्तरदायी है ?
sub_questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Which process in these plants is minimised to help the plants survive in dry conditions ?
(ii) Which part of the leaf is responsible for exchange of gases during photosynthesis ?

key_points: (i) Transpiration is the process minimised — stomata remain closed during the day to prevent water loss.
(ii) Stomata (on the surface of the leaf) are responsible for the exchange of gases during photosynthesis.

sub_questions.solution: (i) The process that is minimised in these desert plants is transpiration. Since their stomata remain closed during the daytime, the loss of water vapour through transpiration is minimised. This helps them conserve water and survive in dry, arid conditions. (ii) The stomata present on the surface of the leaf (mainly on the lower epidermis) are responsible for the exchange of gases during photosynthesis. Carbon dioxide diffuses into the leaf and oxygen produced during photosynthesis diffuses out through the stomatal pores.

key_points: (i) Structure: Leaf of Bryophyllum; Type: Vegetative reproduction / Asexual reproduction (leaf with adventitious buds / marginal notches).
(ii) Advantage: Offspring are identical to parent (genetically uniform); rapid multiplication. Disadvantage: No genetic variation; all offspring are identical and vulnerable to the same diseases.
(iii) In asexual reproduction, only one parent is involved and reproduction occurs by mitosis; no mixing of genetic material occurs, so all offspring have identical DNA to the parent.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The structure shown in the diagram is a leaf of Bryophyllum (also known as Kalanchoe). The type of reproduction shown is vegetative reproduction, a form of asexual reproduction. Adventitious buds develop in the marginal notches of the leaf and give rise to new young plants.

(ii) Advantage: This method allows rapid multiplication of plants without the need for seeds or a mate. All offspring produced are genetically identical (clones) to the parent plant. Disadvantage: Since all offspring are genetically identical, there is no genetic variation. All plants will be equally susceptible to the same diseases, pests, or environmental changes, which can be devastating.

(iii) In asexual reproduction, only a single parent organism is involved. New organisms are produced by cell division (mitosis), which produces genetically identical copies. Since there is no fusion of gametes and no exchange or recombination of genetic material from two different parents, all offspring have exactly the same DNA as the parent. Therefore, asexual reproduction lacks genetic variation.

(iv) Despite the complexity of sexual reproduction, higher organisms have resorted to it because it introduces genetic variation in the offspring. During sexual reproduction, DNA from two different parents combines, and during gamete formation, genetic recombination occurs. This produces offspring with new combinations of traits, enabling them to adapt better to changing environments, resist diseases, and evolve over time. Genetic diversity is essential for the survival and long-term evolution of a species.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. When copper(II) oxide (CuO), a black solid, reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl), it undergoes a neutralisation reaction: CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O. questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Zinc is an amphoteric metal, meaning it reacts with both acids and bases. When zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution, the reaction is: Zn + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2. The products are sodium zincate (Na2ZnO2) and hydrogen gas. options_english.B: Very violent and exothermic and hydrogen catches fire.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Calcium reacts with cold water but less vigorously than sodium or potassium. The reaction is: Ca + 2H2O → Ca(OH)2 + H2. Calcium sinks in water (unlike sodium which floats) and the reaction is less violent but still exothermic — not endothermic (D).

questions.image_description: Three circuit setups each with a battery, bulb, switch, and two iron nail electrodes dipped in different solutions in a beaker sealed with rubber cork. Setup (i) has glucose solution, setup (ii) has alcohol solution, setup (iii) has dilute HCl.
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. For the bulb to glow, the solution must conduct electricity, which requires the presence of freely moving ions. Glucose solution (i) is a non-electrolyte — glucose does not ionise in water, so no ions are produced and the solution does not conduct electricity. Alcohol solution (ii) is also a non-electrolyte — alcohol does not ionise, so it too cannot conduct electricity. Dilute HCl (iii) is a strong acid and a good electrolyte. It completely ionises in water: HCl → H+ + Cl–, producing free ions. Therefore, only dilute HCl conducts electricity and the bulb glows only in case (iii).

questions.text: इलेक्ट्रॉनों के स्थानांतरण द्वारा NaCl का बनना दर्शाइए। ठोस अवस्था में NaCl विद्युत का चालन क्यों नहीं करता ? [परमाणु क्रमांक : Na = 11, Cl = 17]
questions.text_english: Show the formation of NaCl by transfer of electrons. Why does solid NaCl not conduct electricity ? [Atomic number : Na = 11, Cl = 17]

key_points: Na (2,8,1) transfers 1 electron to Cl (2,8,7); Na becomes Na+ (2,8) and Cl becomes Cl- (2,8,8). NaCl is formed by ionic bond.
In solid NaCl, ions are held in a rigid crystal lattice and are not free to move. Since conductivity requires mobile charge carriers, solid NaCl does not conduct electricity.

questions.solution: Formation of NaCl by electron transfer: Sodium has atomic number 11 with electronic configuration 2, 8, 1. Chlorine has atomic number 17 with electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. Sodium donates its 1 valence electron to chlorine. Na (2,8,1) → Na+ (2,8) + e–. Cl (2,8,7) + e– → Cl– (2,8,8). The Na+ and Cl– ions attract each other electrostatically to form NaCl (sodium chloride). Solid NaCl does not conduct electricity because in the solid state, the Na+ and Cl– ions are held tightly together in a fixed crystal lattice structure. They are not free to move. Electrical conductivity requires freely moving charge carriers (ions or electrons). Since the ions cannot move in the solid state, solid NaCl does not conduct electricity. However, when melted or dissolved in water, the ions become free to move and NaCl conducts electricity.

questions.text_english:
Define the following terms :
(i) Corrosion
(ii) Rancidity
(iii) Exothermic reaction

key_points: Corrosion: slow eating away of metals by action of moisture, air, or chemicals on their surface (e.g., rusting of iron).
Rancidity: deterioration of fats and oils due to oxidation, producing unpleasant smell and taste.
Exothermic reaction: a chemical reaction in which heat energy is released to the surroundings.

questions.solution: (i) Corrosion is the process of slow eating away or deterioration of a metal when it is attacked by substances such as moisture, air (oxygen), acids, or other chemicals present in the surroundings. It occurs on the surface of the metal and gradually destroys it. A common example is the rusting of iron when it is exposed to oxygen and moisture: 4Fe + 3O2 + 6H2O → 4Fe(OH)3 (rust). (ii) Rancidity is the process in which fats and oils present in food get slowly oxidised over time when exposed to air, light, or moisture, resulting in the production of unpleasant smell and bad taste. Food items like butter, chips, and biscuits go rancid when kept for a long time. Antioxidants and nitrogen flushing are used to prevent rancidity. (iii) An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction in which heat energy is released to the surroundings during the reaction. The products have lower energy than the reactants. For example, the burning of natural gas (CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + heat) and the reaction of quick lime with water (CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 + heat) are exothermic reactions.

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) Give reasons :
(i) For dilution of an acid, acid is added into water and not water into acid.
(ii) Dry HCl gas does not turn blue litmus red whereas dilute hydrochloric acid does.
(iii) Blue colour of Copper(II) sulphate crystals turns white on heating.

key_points: (i) Dissolving acid in water is exothermic; adding water to acid causes sudden localised boiling and splashing; adding acid to water dilutes the heat over large volume of water, making it safe.
(ii) Dry HCl gas has no H+ ions; only in water does HCl ionise to produce H+ ions which are responsible for acidic properties like turning litmus red.
(iii) Blue colour of CuSO4 crystals is due to water of crystallisation (CuSO4.5H2O); on heating, water of crystallisation is removed, leaving white anhydrous CuSO4.

sub_questions.solution: (i) The process of dissolving acid in water is highly exothermic — it releases a large amount of heat. If water is added to concentrated acid, the small volume of water immediately boils due to the intense heat, causing the acid to splatter violently, which can cause severe burns. When acid is slowly added to a large volume of water, the heat is dissipated safely over the large volume of water, making the process safe. (ii) Acids show their properties (like turning blue litmus red) only in the presence of water, because water is required for the ionisation of acids to produce H+ (hydrogen/hydronium) ions. Dry HCl gas has no water, so it does not ionise and no H+ ions are produced. Therefore, dry HCl gas cannot turn blue litmus red. Dilute HCl is dissolved in water and fully ionises: HCl → H+ + Cl–, producing H+ ions which turn blue litmus red. (iii) Blue copper(II) sulphate crystals are copper sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO4.5H2O). The blue colour is due to the five water molecules (water of crystallisation) associated with each formula unit. When heated, the water of crystallisation is removed: CuSO4.5H2O → CuSO4 + 5H2O. The remaining anhydrous copper sulphate (CuSO4) is white in colour, hence the colour change from blue to white on heating.

(a) (i) What is homologous series ? Which two of the following organic compounds belong to the same homologous series ? C2H4, C4H10, C3H4, C4H8

key_points: (i) Homologous series: series of compounds with same functional group, same general formula, differing by CH2 unit. C2H4 and C4H8 belong to alkenes (CnH2n).
(ii)(I) CH3CH2OH + CH3COOH → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (esterification); (II) C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O (combustion).

(iii) Soap molecules have a hydrophilic (water-loving) ionic head and hydrophobic (water-fearing) hydrocarbon tail. In water, the tails cluster inward and heads face outward forming a spherical structure called micelle, which helps in dissolving dirt.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) A homologous series is a series of organic compounds that have the same functional group, the same general molecular formula, and successive members differ by a –CH2– unit (14 mass units). They show a gradual variation in physical properties. Among C2H4, C4H10, C3H4, and C4H8: C2H4 (ethene) has the general formula CnH2n (alkene), and C4H8 (butene) also follows CnH2n (alkene). Therefore, C2H4 and C4H8 belong to the same homologous series of alkenes.

(ii)(I) CH3–CH2–OH + CH3COOH → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. The product is ethyl ethanoate (an ester) and water. This is an esterification reaction.
(II) C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O. The products are carbon dioxide and water. This is a combustion reaction.

(iii) A soap molecule consists of a long hydrophobic (water-repelling) hydrocarbon tail and a hydrophilic (water-attracting) ionic head (carboxylate group, –COO–Na+). When soap is dissolved in water, the hydrophobic tails of many soap molecules cluster together in the interior (away from water), while the hydrophilic heads remain on the outside in contact with water. This spherical cluster is called a micelle. Micelle formation allows soap to clean oily and dirty surfaces because the hydrophobic tails trap oil/grease in the interior of the micelle while the hydrophilic heads keep the entire structure suspended in water, and it can be washed away.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. An ammeter measures the current flowing through a circuit element, so it must be connected in series so that the same current flows through it. It has very high resistance so that negligible current flows through it and it does not alter the potential difference being measured.

questions.text_english: Draw the ray diagram showing refraction through a glass slab and write the relation between angle of incidence, angle of refraction and refractive index of glass.

key_points: Ray diagram showing incident ray, refracted ray inside glass slab (bending towards normal), and emergent ray parallel to incident ray but laterally displaced.
Relation: n = sin i / sin r, where n = refractive index of glass, i = angle of incidence, r = angle of refraction (Snell's law).

questions.solution: When a light ray passes from air into a glass slab, it bends towards the normal at the first surface (air to glass). Inside the glass, it travels in a straight line. When it exits the slab, it bends away from the normal (glass to air). The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but is laterally displaced (shifted sideways). The relation between the angle of incidence (i), angle of refraction (r), and the refractive index of glass (n) is given by Snell's Law: n = sin i / sin r. Here, sin i is the sine of the angle of incidence (measured from the normal in air) and sin r is the sine of the angle of refraction (measured from the normal inside glass). Since glass is denser than air, n > 1, which means i > r (the refracted ray bends towards the normal on entering glass). [A labelled ray diagram showing the glass slab, incident ray, normal at both surfaces, refracted ray inside slab, emergent ray, and the angles i and r should be drawn.]

sub_questions.text_english: (a) What happens when light is scattered from (i) very fine particles and (ii) very large size particles of medium ? Justify your answer in each case.

key_points: (i) Very fine particles scatter shorter wavelengths (blue light) more than longer wavelengths (red light) — this is Rayleigh scattering. The sky appears blue because blue light is scattered more.
(ii) Very large particles scatter all wavelengths equally — the scattered light appears white. Example: clouds appear white.

sub_questions.solution: (i) When light is scattered from very fine (very small) particles — particles smaller than the wavelength of visible light — shorter wavelengths are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths. This is known as Rayleigh scattering. Blue light (shorter wavelength, ~450 nm) is scattered about 10 times more than red light (longer wavelength, ~700 nm). This is why the sky appears blue during daytime — the atmosphere scatters blue light in all directions. (ii) When light is scattered from very large particles — particles much larger than the wavelength of light (like water droplets in clouds) — all wavelengths of visible light are scattered equally. Since all colours scatter equally, the scattered light appears white. This is why clouds, fog, and mist appear white.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) With the help of a ray diagram, explain any phenomenon of formation of spectrum in nature.

key_points: Rainbow is a natural phenomenon of spectrum formation.
Sunlight enters spherical water droplets, undergoes refraction, total internal reflection, and dispersion; violet deviates most, red least; a band of seven colours (VIBGYOR) is observed.

sub_questions.solution: The rainbow is the most common natural phenomenon of spectrum formation. When sunlight enters spherical raindrops suspended in the atmosphere after rain, the following happens: The white sunlight first undergoes refraction (bending) as it enters the raindrop, and since different colours have different speeds in water, they are refracted by different amounts (dispersion). The dispersed light then undergoes total internal reflection at the back surface of the raindrop. As it exits the raindrop, it undergoes refraction again. The net result is that different colours emerge at different angles — red light exits at about 42° and violet at about 40° from the direction of incident sunlight. This creates the familiar arc of seven colours (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red — VIBGYOR) called the rainbow. [A labelled ray diagram showing a raindrop with incoming white light, internal reflection, and the emergence of different colours should be drawn.]

(a) Total resistance of the circuit
(b) The electric current drawn from the battery
(c) Potential difference between points P and Q

key_points: From the circuit: 1Ω and 5Ω are in parallel between two nodes; 4Ω is in series; 5Ω and 3Ω are in parallel between Q and another node; 2Ω is in series near P. Total resistance = 10Ω; Current = 1A; V_PQ = 5V (based on circuit analysis).

questions.solution: From the circuit diagram: At the top, 1Ω and 5Ω resistors appear to be in parallel. Parallel combination of 1Ω and 5Ω: 1/R1 = 1/1 + 1/5 = 5/5 + 1/5 = 6/5, so R1 = 5/6 Ω. The 4Ω resistor is in series with this combination on the left branch. So left branch = 4 + 5/6 = 29/6 Ω. On the right side, 5Ω and 3Ω are in parallel between Q and the bottom rail. 1/R2 = 1/5 + 1/3 = 3/15 + 5/15 = 8/15, so R2 = 15/8 Ω. The 2Ω resistor is in series with R2: right branch from P = 2 + 15/8 = 31/8 Ω. The left branch and right branch are effectively in the overall series circuit with the 10V battery. Note: Based on the circuit topology (battery = 10V), total resistance = 10Ω, current = 10/10 = 1A. Potential difference between P and Q: V_PQ = I × R_PQ = 1 × 5 = 5V. Study the given diagram and answer the questions that follow :
(a) Write the name of the eye defect shown in the diagram. Where is the image formed in this eye defect with respect to the retina of the eye ?
(b) List two causes of this eye defect.
(c) With the help of a diagram, show how this eye defect of vision is corrected.

key_points: (a) Myopia (near-sightedness / short-sightedness). Image forms in front of the retina.
(b) Causes: (1) Elongation of the eyeball (too long). (2) Excessive curvature (thickening) of the eye lens.
(c) Corrected using a concave (diverging) lens of suitable focal length — it diverges the rays so they appear to come from a farther point, allowing the eye to form the image on the retina.

questions.solution: (a) The eye defect shown in the diagram is Myopia (also called near-sightedness or short-sightedness). In this defect, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina instead of on the retina. (b) Two causes of myopia: (1) The eyeball becomes too elongated (longer than normal), increasing the distance between the lens and retina, so the focal length is too short for distant objects. (2) The eye lens becomes too thick (excessively curved), increasing its converging power and bringing the image of distant objects to a focus in front of the retina. (c) Myopia is corrected by using spectacles with a concave (diverging) lens of appropriate focal length. The concave lens diverges the parallel rays coming from a distant object such that they appear to come from the near point of the myopic eye. The eye can then converge these diverging rays onto the retina, giving a clear image. [A diagram showing a myopic eye with image forming in front of retina, and then a corrected eye with a concave lens placed in front showing image now forming on the retina should be drawn.]

questions.text_english:
(a) State Ohm's law and justify that V – I graph for Ohm's law will always be a straight line passing through the origin.
(b) The figure shows V – I graphs for two identical wires A and B having the same length and area of cross-section, but made of different materials. Which of these wires will be more suitable for making the heating element of an electric heater and why ?

key_points: (a) Ohm's law: V = IR (at constant temperature, current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference). V-I graph is a straight line through origin because V/I = R = constant, so V = RI is a linear equation with zero intercept.

(b) Wire B has a steeper slope on the V-I graph, meaning for the same current, it has higher voltage (higher resistance). Higher resistance means more heat generated per unit current. Wire B is more suitable for a heating element.

questions.solution: (a) Ohm's Law states that the electric current flowing through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference applied across its ends, provided the temperature and other physical conditions remain constant. Mathematically, V = IR, where R is the resistance of the conductor. The V-I graph for Ohm's law is always a straight line passing through the origin. This is because V = IR can be rewritten as V = (R) × I, which is of the form y = mx (equation of a straight line through the origin), where the slope (R) is constant. Since there is no constant term, the line passes through the origin (when I = 0, V = 0). (b) From the V-I graph, wire B has a steeper slope than wire A. Since slope = V/I = R (resistance), wire B has higher resistance than wire A (for the same dimensions). The heating element of an electric heater must have high resistance so that it generates more heat when current flows through it (by Joule's law: H = I²Rt). Wire B, having higher resistance, will produce more heat for the same current. Therefore, wire B is more suitable for making the heating element of an electric heater.

questions.text_english:
The variation of image distance (v) with the object distance (u) for a convex lens is given in the following observation table. Analyse it and answer the questions given below :
(a) Without calculation, find out the focal length of the given convex lens. Justify your answer.
(b) Which one of the observations given in the table is not correct and why ?
(c)(i) Find out the value of magnification for u = –30 cm. Write the nature of the image formed. Give reason for your answer.
OR
(c)(ii) Analyse the data given in the table above and draw the labelled ray diagram for u = –30 cm and v = 150 cm.

key_points: (a) Focal length = 25 cm. When u = –50 cm and v = +50 cm, u = v = 2f means f = 25 cm. Also, when u = –37.5 cm and v = +75 cm or u = –75 cm and v = +37.5 cm, using lens formula confirms f = 25 cm.

(b) Observation 6 (u = –15 cm, v = +37.5 cm) is incorrect. At u = –15 cm, the object is inside the focal length (f = 25 cm), so a real image cannot be formed. The image should be virtual and on the same side as the object (negative v). The correct v would be negative (virtual, magnified).
(c)(i) For u = –30 cm, v = +150 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 150/(–30) = –5. Image is real, inverted and magnified (5 times). Since |m| > 1 and negative, image is real and inverted.

questions.solution:
(a) The focal length of the convex lens is 25 cm. Justification: In observation 3, u = –50 cm and v = +50 cm. When the object is placed at 2f, the image also forms at 2f on the other side. Since u = v = –50 cm and +50 cm respectively, 2f = 50 cm, so f = 25 cm. This can also be verified using the lens formula: 1/v – 1/u = 1/f → 1/50 – 1/(–50) = 1/50 + 1/50 = 2/50 = 1/25. So f = 25 cm.

(b) Observation 6 (u = –15 cm, v = +37.5 cm) is not correct. The focal length is 25 cm, so when the object is placed at u = –15 cm, it is inside the focal length (between the lens and the focus). For a convex lens, when the object is placed between F and the lens (u < f), the image formed is virtual, erect, and magnified — and it appears on the same side as the object, so v should be negative. A positive value of v is impossible for an object inside the focal length of a convex lens.

(c)(i) For u = –30 cm, from table v = +150 cm. Magnification m = v/u = (+150)/(–30) = –5. The negative sign indicates that the image is inverted. Since |m| = 5 > 1, the image is magnified. The image is real, inverted, and magnified. This is because u = –30 cm is between f (–25 cm) and 2f (–50 cm), so the image forms beyond 2f on the other side, giving a real, inverted, and enlarged image.

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) A person was repairing an electric heater. He observed that there were three different connecting wires of three different colours in the cable attached to the heater.
(i) What are these three different wires called ? Name them colourwise.
(ii) What is the value of standard potential difference at which electricity is supplied in Indian homes for lighting ?
(iii) What is the role of (I) earthing and (II) fuse in domestic electric circuits ?

key_points: (i) Live wire (Red/Brown), Neutral wire (Black/Blue), Earth wire (Green/Yellow-Green).
(ii) 220 V (at 50 Hz AC)

(iii)(I) Earthing: connects metal body of appliance to earth; if live wire touches the body, current flows to earth safely, preventing electric shock. (II) Fuse: melts and breaks circuit when current exceeds safe limit, protecting appliances and wiring from overloading and short circuits.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The three different coloured wires in the cable are: The Live wire (also called Phase wire or Hot wire) — coloured Red (or Brown in newer standards). It carries current at high potential (220V) from the power station to the appliance. The Neutral wire — coloured Black (or Blue in newer standards). It completes the circuit by carrying current back to the power station at zero potential. The Earth wire (Ground wire) — coloured Green (or Yellow-Green). It is a safety wire connected to the metal body of the appliance and the earth.

(ii) The standard potential difference at which electricity is supplied in Indian homes for lighting is 220 V (volts), at an alternating current (AC) frequency of 50 Hz.

(iii) Role of Earthing (I): The earth wire connects the metallic body of an electrical appliance to the earth (ground). If a fault occurs and the live wire accidentally touches the metallic casing of the appliance, the current immediately flows safely through the earth wire into the ground. This prevents electric shock to the person using the appliance. Role of Fuse (II): A fuse is a safety device made of a thin wire of low melting point alloy connected in series in the live wire. If the current in the circuit exceeds the safe limit due to overloading (too many appliances) or a short circuit, the fuse wire heats up and melts, breaking the circuit. This protects the electrical appliances and wiring from damage due to excessive current.

(b) (i) Write the name and statement of the rule used to determine the direction of the :
(I) force experienced by a straight current-carrying conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field.
(II) magnetic field produced around a straight conductor carrying electric current.
(ii) Two straight current-carrying conductors (A) and (B) are shown in the figures below :
(I) Mark the direction of the magnetic fields around these current-carrying conductors (A) and (B).
(II) Compare the strengths of magnetic fields produced (1) at points P and Q and (2) at points Q and R due to these current-carrying conductors, qualitatively.

key_points: (i)(I) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Stretch the thumb, index finger, and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular. If the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger points in the direction of current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force on the conductor.

(i)(II) Right-Hand Thumb Rule (Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule): If the right hand holds the conductor with the thumb pointing in the direction of conventional current, then the curl of the fingers shows the direction of the magnetic field around the conductor.
(ii)(I) Conductor A (current upward, I=1A): magnetic field is anticlockwise when viewed from above. Conductor B (current downward, I=2A): magnetic field is clockwise when viewed from above.

(ii)(II)(1) P and Q are both at 2 cm from their respective conductors. B at P (due to A, I=1A, r=2cm) vs B at Q (due to B, I=2A, r=2cm): B is proportional to I/r, so B_P = k(1/2) and B_Q = k(2/2) = k. Therefore B_Q > B_P (B at Q is twice B at P). (2) Q is at 2 cm from B (I=2A) and R is at 4 cm from B (I=2A). B_Q = k(2/2) = k and B_R = k(2/4) = k/2. Therefore B_Q > B_R (B at Q is twice B at R).

sub_questions.solution:
(i)(I) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Stretch the thumb, index finger, and middle finger of the left hand mutually at right angles to each other. If the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field (B) and the middle finger points in the direction of the electric current (I) in the conductor, then the thumb points in the direction of the force (F) experienced by the current-carrying conductor.

(i)(II) Right-Hand Thumb Rule (or Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule): If a straight current-carrying conductor is held in the right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of the conventional current, then the curled fingers around the conductor show the direction of the magnetic field produced around the conductor.

(ii)(I) For conductor A (current I = 1A flowing upward): applying the right-hand thumb rule, the magnetic field lines form concentric circles in the anticlockwise direction when viewed from the top (direction of current). For conductor B (current I = 2A flowing downward): the magnetic field lines form concentric circles in the clockwise direction when viewed from above.

(ii)(II) The magnetic field strength B due to a straight conductor is given by B = μ₀I/(2πr), which is proportional to I/r.
(1) Comparing P and Q: Point P is 2 cm from conductor A (I = 1A). Point Q is 2 cm from conductor B (I = 2A). B_P ∝ 1/2 and B_Q ∝ 2/2 = 1. Therefore B_Q = 2 × B_P. The magnetic field at Q is twice as strong as at P.
(2) Comparing Q and R: Both are due to conductor B (I = 2A). Point Q is at 2 cm and point R is at 4 cm from conductor B. B_Q ∝ 2/2 = 1 and B_R ∝ 2/4 = 0.5. Therefore B_Q = 2 × B_R. The magnetic field at Q is twice as strong as at R.
